chapter: Woody Herman, Henderson and the Indiana Theater
title: Leading the small stage band at the Indiana Theater in 1941
summary: He took the band onstage at the theater at 43rd and Indiana after the singer Lamille, with saxophone, drums and piano, sometimes himself playing both trumpet and piano.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: When did you take the band into the Indiana Theater?

I took the band in the Indiana Theater -- who did they have there? A girl by the name of Lamille and she left. I played under her, played under Lamille. This was -- I don't remember those dates back then. Let's see, all right. I have to go to thinking about residence, then maybe (that was still, and I left) that'll bring it -- I was living at 3730 (inaudible), round about 1941.
'41 you went to the band there?
And what did you play, stage shows?
It was like a pit band, or a house band?

Onstage. Yeah, onstage, (we were in the background) behind the -- the audience could see us, all right, but we'd be behind the performers. And, listen, it wasn't really a big band. [Eisley], saxophone, --
Bill Eiseley, saxophone, and Slaughter was the drummer one time, and this same lady that was with my band was on piano.

Yeah, uh-huh. And myself on the trumpet. And then one time, before I had this lady, as my pianist, I had -- I would have different men that I would give the job to. I had Joe, John Johnson-- I had a bass player that played bass and played piano.
Yeah, he's a good friend of mine.

And so, he got a gig one night. He got a gig for piano one night, and he played -- no, he got a gig for bass, playing bass one night, because they were short a bass. And so that left me without a piano.

And I had to -- yeah, and I had to play -- and of course the manager of the theater was laughing. He says, one time he'd see me on the horn and the next time he'd see me on the piano. Because I picked the drums and saxophone, I could play the opening, and if someone could sing
I'd get to the piano, and I'd be on the piano, and you'd see first he's next he's first he's faces over here, faces over there, and faces overthere, and next he's faces over there.
